By producing affordable reusable sanitary pads and raising awareness in schools, she hopes to make menstrual health more accessible and help girls stay in class. Report by Awa Diouf & Guillaume Gougeon.

title: Guinea bans Burkina Faso broadcaster, escalating diplomatic tensions
summary: Tensions rise between Guinea and Burkina Faso after Conakry bans Burkinabe broadcaster RTB, amid a diplomatic dispute over gold miners and a caricature of President Mamadi Doumbouya. summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe said the Trump administration had "an unbalanced approach" in implementing the DR Congo peace deal it brokered. Finally, he defended a deal for Rwanda to host failed asylum seekers from five European countries.

summary: Nigeria has moved a step closer to letting its 36 states set up their own police forces. The National Assembly has sent a constitutional amendment bill to the president, as authorities seek state-run police to complement the federal force amid growing insecurity. Many states currently fund vigilante groups to fight armed groups like Boko Haram, but these groups are poorly trained and ill-equipped for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent has the latest.

title: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from Senegal's ruling party

title: Predictable: DR Congo-Rwanda rivalry spills over to Francophonie summit

Clark says that "nobody expected Rwanda to back down in this way" following President Emmanuel Macron's request that President Paul Kagame withdraw Louise Mushikiwabo's candidacy for a third term as head of the group.

title: Rwanda to host hub for rejected EU migrants
summary: In tonight's edition: Five European countries are negotiating a deal to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. title: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
summary: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.

title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
summary: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.

title: Cape Verde's President José Maria Neves wins second term
summary: Cape Verde's President Jose Maria Neves won re-election on Sunday with 63.8 percent of votes cast, provisional electoral commission results showed. Neves had been the favourite in the West African archipelago. His main challenger was Joana Rosa Amado, the country's first woman presidential candidate, who conceded and congratulated Neves Monday morning.

title: Guinea opens illegal gold mining trial, 1,200 people arrested
summary: Guinea opened a trial over illegal gold mining on Thursday, November 12, after a crackdown on mineral extraction in the district of Siguiri. There was a ban on "unregulated and illegal" gold mining in the area where the military was subsequently deployed. Security forces have expelled tens of thousands of foreign nationals who had come to work in the region's mines.

title: Toera's homecoming: Madagascar's slain king joins his ancestors after 129 years
summary: In 1897, French colonial troops killed King Toera, ruler of Madagascar's powerful Sakalava kingdom of Menabe, and took his skull to Paris, where it remained hidden in a museum for more than a century. France returned the remains last year, and for the first time since his death, King Toera took his place among his ancestors during the Sakalava people's most sacred ritual.

title: Amnesty criticises South Sudan, UN over failure to heed massacre warnings
summary: Amnesty International said Thursday, November 12, that South Sudan and UN peacekeepers failed to act on warnings of a massacre that ended with more than 200 dead in March. The world's youngest country has been plagued by civil war, poverty, corruption and intercommunal violence since it was formed in 2011. FRANCE 24 spoke to Donatella Rovera, Senior crisis response adviser at Amnesty International.

title: Across Africa: Tunisians drawn into Russia's war with Ukraine
summary: This week: A new report says more than 1,400 Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023. Also, as South Africa races to become Africa's digital gateway, a growing backlash is emerging in Cape Town. Plus music, dance and theatre lit up Abéché as the city's arts festival in Chad drew crowds of young spectators.

title: NGO criticises UN's response to massacre in South Sudan
summary: In tonight's edition: Amnesty International accuses both the government and UN peacekeepers of failing to protect civilians during a massacre in South Sudan that killed over 200 people. Also, more than a thousand people are prosecuted for illegal mining in Guinea. Plus a century after French colonial troops killed him, a Malagasy king has finally come home.

title: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake
summary: A viral video appearing to show China's Xi Jinping "snubbing" Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit has racked up millions of views, fuelling speculation about tensions between Beijing and Moscow. But the footage is fake. FRANCE 24 traced the original video to an earlier summit, where the two leaders did shake hands. The creator, who runs a satire account, admitted to manipulating the footage using Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI, as Vedika Bahl explains.

title: 'Friends' But Who Benefits? Notes from an Historic Summit, Myanmar's Genocide Ruling, Time to 'Bre-join' the EU?
summary: Welcome to the World This Week with Gavin Lee. You give us 45 minutes, we'll give you 7 days worth of crystal clear analysis. As ever, alongside a handpicked panel of four distinguished foreign correspondents.

title: Bangladesh: Hasina supporters vandalise ruling party office
summary: Hundreds of supporters of ousted Bangladesh premier Sheikh Hasina staged street protests on Thursday, as a wave of arson attacks escalated tensions ahead of her planned return from exile next month.

summary: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "f

title: Xi demonstrating China's 'global status', occupying 'central position' in relation to Trump & Putin
summary: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Rex Li, professor of international relations at King's College London. For Professor Li, the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in China is less about "reaching concrete agreements and a common position." Rather, he argues, it is about demonstrating Xi's ability to bring the American and Russian leaders together to discuss major geopolitical issues. title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
summary: In August 2017, after attacks by a Rohingya militia, Myanmar’s army launched a “clearance campaign” in Rakhine state, with survivors describing mass killings, rapes and burned villages as hundreds of thousands fled to Bangladesh. The Gambia took Myanmar to the ICJ in 2019, and after a seven-year legal fight the court has ruled that Myanmar committed acts of genocide. Meanwhile some 1.2 million Rohingya remain in crowded camps, unable to return home.

title: China summit ends with little new, Europe backs Ukraine in Berlin
summary: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia met in Shenzhen for a historic first, but the summit brought little new: non-binding statements on peace and no plan to meet regularly. In Berlin, Europeans gathered to show their support for Ukraine, a pointed answer to a summit where Europe had no seat, as FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

title: In South Korea, women forced into prostitution on US military bases seek justice
summary: Tens of thousands of women were forced to work in South Korean state-sanctioned brothels used by American soldiers based in the country after the Korean War. They were raped, physically abused and forcibly confined. Now, after decades of silence, some of these women are speaking out.

title: 'Their lives, their rights, their history': Not the end of accountability for the Rohingya people'
summary: Oliver Farry welcomes Sonya Sceats, Director and CEO of the British Institute of International and Comparative Law. The case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar before the ICJ, and the court ruling, both have great significance for the Rohingya people, the interpretation of the Genocide Convention and the possibility of future criminal proceedings. The case could also have important implications for South Africa's proceedings against Israel, where there are “many similarities between the two cases.”

title: What to know about Xi, Putin and Trump's historic trilateral summit
summary: China's Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump met for a historic summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, where they agreed on a "peace declaration". title: Myanmar's Rohingya case: how does the ICJ define genocide?

title: Xi, Trump, Putin: historic summit ends, outcome unclear
summary: The unprecedented trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin ended on Thursday in Shenzhen after about an hour and 20 minutes. No details have emerged yet, but the three leaders talking face to face is already an event. Each has their own agenda: Putin wants to be back on the world stage, Trump needs a win at home, and Xi is asserting China’s status as an economic superpower. What comes out of it remains unclear, as FRANCE 24's journalists explain.

title: APEC Summit: Trump, Putin, Xi hold 'historic' meeting

title: South Korea tightens security for national exam over AI cheating scandal
summary: More than 550,000 candidates sat South Korea’s Suneung university entrance exam under extraordinary security, after an AI cheating scandal in which a top scorer on a national tax accountant exam admitted using a hidden mini camera to send questions to an AI system. Authorities inspected students’ glasses, deployed thousands of extra supervisors and ordered stickers over every button on candidates’ clothing. A nationwide disaster alert was also sent to make even muted phones buzz, exposing any devices smuggled into exam rooms.

title: Nuclear arms at the center of the Shenzhen trilateral meeting
summary: Nuclear weapons are at the top of Donald Trump’s agenda at the trilateral summit in Beijing. summary: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. title: Trump, Xi, Putin summit: What was it all about?
summary: Donald Trump has left China after a historic first meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Ukraine was discussed without Kyiv or European leaders in the room, which raised eyebrows, though Trump defended dialogue with rivals and Putin said the talks created conditions for future agreements. Xi warned major powers against conflict, and topics included reducing nuclear risks, reforming the UN and increasing energy flows.

title: Haiti: Salvador’s Bukele publishes video of attack on gang leader’s house
summary: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday that his troops demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as Jeff Gwo Lwa. "My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières," Bukele wrote on X - referencing a 1803 battle critical in helping secure Haiti's independence from France.

title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
summary: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

title: Hegseth makes surprise trip to Venezuela, renews military cooperation
summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announcing a resumption of military cooperation with Venezuela and vowing to crack down on drug traffickers. The trip marks the highest-level US visit since the ouster of Nicolas Maduro in January, signalling a dramatic shift in relations between the two countries.

title: US judge strikes down Trump visa restrictions on foreign students, journalists

title: November 17 blackout hoax: How a conspiracy theory went viral around the world
summary: A conspiracy theory claiming a worldwide "blackout" will hit the world on November 17 has spread across social media, with the claim it will cut electricity, internet and banking services. The rumour stems from a routine US FEMA emergency alert test, but was amplified by cryptocurrency accounts, misleading claims about EU preparedness advice and references to "The Simpsons". Recent technology outages, flight disruptions and cyberattacks have added to public anxiety, helping turn a routine test into a global hoax.

title: Pope concludes South America homecoming, reassures faithful after cancer scare
summary: Pope Leo XIV finished Monday his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru reiterating his advocacy for social justice, environmental protection and the importance of community. Just a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery, the 71-year-old pontiff drew millions of faithful across South America, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.

title: The new faces of the US Congress
summary: The United States Congress is about to welcome dozens of new faces. A majority of them, Democratic, after the "blue wave" in the midterm elections. FRANCE 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson catches up with one of these new lawmakers as they go through orientation as they prepare to take office in January. He speaks with Katy Padilla Stout, U.S. Representative-elect for Texas's 23rd congressional district.

title: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait
summary: The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, with Iran attacking vessels attempting to cross it. As concerns grow over the environmental impact of the war, with toxic chemicals spreading through the air and sea, one swimmer and ocean advocate has gone a step further than issuing warnings: he plunged into the polluted and dangerous waters of the strait, calling on all sides to end the conflict.

title: Houthis launch strikes on Saudi Arabia
summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen continue to exchange strikes with the Saudi-led coalition. The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh early on Saturday. It marks the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in recent days, following Saudi-led strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. Yuka Royer has the latest.

title: Yemen's Houthis target Riyadh after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched strikes on Riyadh on Saturday after Saudi-led coalition air raids on Yemen, escalating a months-long surge in cross-border attacks.

title: Skyscraper in Riyadh damaged as Saudi Arabia reports surge in new Houthi attacks
summary: A skyscraper in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh was damaged on Thursday after the Gulf country reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis. Witnesses said the city's Public Investment Fund Tower, which showcases Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions, was "damaged across several floors, with windows blown out".

title: Gaza: Israel launched new offensive on Nuseirat
summary: Israeli tanks have moved east of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, with witnesses reporting heavy shelling, gunfire and airstrikes as the Israeli military says it has launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area. Strikes killed at least three people on Wednesday, and displaced families are fleeing again, saying there is no real ceasefire. Israel and Hamas accuse each other of breaking the truce in force since October 2025, while Gadi Eisenkot tries to form a government after inconclusive elections.

title: Middle East crisis poses 'largest threat' to energy security in history, warns IEA
summary: The International Energy Agency said on Thursday that the Middle East crisis triggered by US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February posed the “largest threat” to energy security in history. It warned that consumers were bearing more of the costs as Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted oil shipments.

title: Israeli army launches ground operation in Hamas-controlled area of Gaza
summary: The Israeli military said it had launched an operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, where an AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp. The rare ground operation comes after inconclusive Israeli elections, with the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot trying to form a government without caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

title: Writer Etgar Keret: 'The Israel my parents dreamed of' is still possible, but not under Netanyahu
summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Israeli writer and filmmaker Etgar Keret, author of "The Seven Good Years". Keret argues that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking to remain in power, at any cost, including delegitimising Arab parties and prolonging conflict. "For him, it could be a never-ending war as long as he's in power. He has no incentive to stop it," our guest warns.

title: Did the US use ‘blackout bombs’ in Iran? Images reveal mysterious fibres at infrastructure sites
summary: Photographs published by Iranian local media suggest that US forces may have used graphite bombs, also known as ‘blackout bombs’, against infrastructure in Iran in recent days. These weapons are designed to disrupt electricity supplies by causing short circuits rather than physically destroying power facilities.

title: Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as government forces retreat to defend their capital
summary: Houthi forces in Yemen have advanced to within 60 kilometres of Aden, the seat of the country's internationally recognised government, military and government sources said Sunday. The embattled government earlier announced it was pulling back its last forces from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend its temporary capital on the southern coast of Yemen.

title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
summary: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.

summary: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama.
